# Java

<!-- Generated by bazel run //tools/docs/languages:languages_bin -- --write from java/lang.json and java/defs.bzl. Do not edit. -->

This page helps you build, test and check Java code with rules_dx.

## Quick start

`MODULE.bazel` sits at the root of your repository and lists the Bazel modules, meaning external dependencies, that your project uses. Add `rules_dx` to it:

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

Then let dx set up the rest, as in the [Quickstart](../../README.md#quickstart):

```sh
bazel run @rules_dx//:dx -- init --apply
```

For a Java project, `MODULE.bazel` then looks like this:

```python
module(name = "my_project")

bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

A `BUILD.bazel` file declares targets: the libraries, binaries and tests that Bazel builds. This one is a small Java package from [`java/tests/consumer`](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/java/tests/consumer/BUILD.bazel):

```python
load("@rules_dx//java:defs.bzl", "java_library", "java_test")

java_library(
    name = "my_project",
    srcs = ["Greet.java"],
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)

java_test(
    name = "greet_test",
    size = "small",
    srcs = ["GreetTest.java"],
    test_class = "consumer.GreetTest",
    deps = [":my_project"],
)
```

Build and test everything. `//...` means every target in the repository:

```sh
tools/dx test //...
```

## Dependencies

List the artifacts in a rules_jvm_external `maven_install.json` and run
`dx generate --apply`. The `java` language of `dx generate` writes the targets and `deps`.
A dependency is the label `@maven//:<group>_<artifact>`, with dots and dashes
turned into underscores, for example `@maven//:com_google_guava_guava`. See
[generate](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/docs/cli/commands/generate.md).

### Writing targets

Warnings fail the build unless a target turns that off.

`java_binary` and `java_test` infer `main_class` and `test_class` from the
sources and the package path. Set them to override. Without `srcs`, or with
`select()` srcs, the class comes from the package path. If the package path
has no Java root, the build fails and asks for `test_class` or `main_class`.

## Quality

By default `dx format` runs `google_java_format`, `dx lint` runs `pmd`,
`spotbugs` and `typos`, and `dx typecheck` runs `javac`. `pmd` reads a ruleset bound
with `pmd_config`. Without one it reports unused private methods, fields, locals,
parameters and assignments as info. See the
[quality config table](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/docs/cli/commands/quality.md).

## Bench and fuzz

`java_bench` runs JMH benchmarks for `dx bench`. JMH 1.37 comes with rules_dx, so no Maven hub entries are needed.

```python
load("@rules_dx//java:defs.bzl", "java_bench")

java_bench(
    name = "sum_bench",
    srcs = ["Sum.java"],
)
```

The test is tagged `dx-bench`, runs in the default test set and writes `dx-bench.json` with one row per `@Benchmark` method. It runs one warmup and three measurement iterations of 200 ms in the test JVM, without forking. `kotlin_bench` in `@rules_dx//kotlin:defs.bzl` and `scala_bench` in `@rules_dx//scala:defs.bzl` take Kotlin and Scala sources the same way. `size`, `timeout`, `args`, `env`, `flaky`, `jvm_flags`, `data` and `visibility` go to the test. Other attributes go to the library that compiles `srcs`. `tags` and `target_compatible_with` go to every target.

## Rules

`load` brings rules into a `BUILD.bazel` file. Load the ones you use from `@rules_dx//java:defs.bzl`:

```python
load("@rules_dx//java:defs.bzl", "java_library", "java_binary", "java_test")
```

### `java_library`

```python
java_library(name, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Minimal wrapper over java_library.

### `java_binary`

```python
java_binary(name, *, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Wrapper over java_binary that infers main_class.

### `java_test`

```python
java_test(name, *, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Wrapper over java_test that infers test_class.

### `java_fuzz_test`

```python
java_fuzz_test(name, *, srcs = None, target_class = None, deps = None, visibility = None, tags = None, **kwargs)
```

A Jazzer fuzz target plus a runner for dx fuzz.

### `java_bench`

```python
java_bench(name, *, srcs, deps = None, tags = None, **kwargs)
```

Runs the JMH benchmarks in srcs and writes dx-bench.json for dx bench.

## Tools and package files

dx runs these tools and reads these package files for Java:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Tools | `google_java_format`, `javac`, `pmd`, `spotbugs` |
| Ecosystems | maven |
| Manifests | `libs.versions.toml` |
| Lockfiles | `maven_install.json` |

## Platforms

Java builds and tests on:

- Linux arm64
- Linux x86_64
- macOS arm64
- Windows arm64
- Windows x86_64

See the [support matrix](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/docs/support-matrix.md).

## API docs

`tools/dx docs` builds the API docs with `javadoc`; see [docs](../cli/commands/docs.md).

To declare a docs target yourself, load the rule behind it:

```python
load("@rules_dx//tools/docs/jvm:defs.bzl", "java_doc_shard")
```

### `java_doc_shard`

```python
java_doc_shard(name, lib, package = "", deps = [], **kwargs)
```

Declares the DocIr shard of one Java library.
